summary.en: Select build variants with #if families, distinguish defined from enabled, and keep platform assumptions explicit.
summary.bn: #if দিয়ে বিল্ডের ভিন্ন কোড বেছে নাও, ম্যাক্রো আছে আর চালু আছে—এই পার্থক্য বুঝো, প্ল্যাটফর্মের শর্ত স্পষ্ট রাখো।

notes: These complete programs target C17; declarations in loops require C99 or later.

examples.title: A defined flag can still be disabled
examples.explanationHtml: DEBUG exists with value zero, so the program prints defined and disabled messages.

examples.title: Identify a documented platform convention
examples.explanationHtml: The recorded execution reports the actual supported platform branch.
examples.outputNote: The message depends on platform macro conventions; this .out records the actual Linux run.

examples.title: Enable traces with a build flag
examples.explanationHtml: With -DDEBUG=1 the trace is included before the unchanged result line.

practice.title: Use a default room capacity
practice.statementHtml: Read people from 0 to 100. Print People: then 1 for at most 30, otherwise 0. Define ROOM_CAPACITY as 30 only if the build has not already defined it.
hints: Use #ifndef for the default and a runtime comparison for people.

practice.title: Keep an enabled debug trace
practice.statementHtml: Define DEBUG as one. Read value from -100 to 100. Print Value:, then trace, then twice the value, each on its own line.
hints: The trace is selected by #if DEBUG.

practice.title: Choose a compile-time multiplier
practice.statementHtml: Define LEVEL as two. Read base from 0 to 20. Print Base: then base times the selected multiplier: two for level one, three for level two, otherwise four.
hints: An #elif group selects exactly one multiplier declaration.

practice.title: Combine feature flags
practice.statementHtml: Define FEATURE_A as one and FEATURE_B as zero. Read value from -20 to 20. Print Base value: then value+10 when A is enabled and B disabled, otherwise value.
hints: Use a preprocessing logical condition on the flags.

quiz.prompt: Does #ifdef DEBUG select its branch when DEBUG is defined as zero?
quiz.explanation: #ifdef checks existence rather than the replacement value.
options: Only if DEBUG is an enum

quiz.prompt: Which form tests a zero-or-one numeric enable flag?
quiz.explanation: #if interprets the expanded integer condition as false or true.

quiz.prompt: Why use #ifndef around a configuration default?
quiz.explanation: The source supplies a value only when the build has not supplied one.
options: To preserve an existing build definition

quiz.explanation: Preprocessing conditions do not inspect ordinary C type expressions.

quiz.prompt: What does a typo in a #if identifier often become?
quiz.explanation: Remaining identifiers are replaced with zero, so -Wundef can help.

quiz.prompt: Which macro is guaranteed by C17 as a Linux detector?
quiz.explanation: Operating-system macro names are implementation conventions.
options: No such standard detector is required

quiz.prompt: What should debug-only code avoid doing?
quiz.explanation: Removing traces should not remove required program work.
options: Essential state changes needed for correctness

quiz.prompt: Which presence and value messages print for DEBUG defined as zero?
quiz.explanation: Presence is true while the numeric value is false.

quiz.prompt: Which ordered room threshold matches the configured size thirty?
quiz.explanation: Thirty fails fifty but meets twenty.

quiz.prompt: What default debug output remains without a command-line override?
quiz.explanation: The source default sets DEBUG to zero while preserving the essential result.

keyPoints.en: Platform macro spellings come from implementation conventions.

keyPoints.bn: সমর্থিত প্রতিটি কোডের বিকল্প সত্যি কম্পাইল করে দেখো।

examQuestions.question: Contrast #ifdef DEBUG with #if DEBUG when DEBUG is zero.
examQuestions.answerHtml: #ifdef is true because DEBUG is defined. #if expands its value to zero and is false. Choose presence checks for existence-only markers and value checks for numeric enable flags.

examQuestions.question: Explain a safe debug/release configuration using a default and build override.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Wrap a default DEBUG=0 definition in #ifndef DEBUG. A build can pass -DDEBUG=1 to include trace lines under #if DEBUG. Keep essential calculations outside those trace branches. Build and run both variants, verifying the same core result and only the intended extra diagnostics. Use consistent flags across related files.
